findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Including I18n::Backend::Fallbacks into the backend for every environment (line 9) makes every backend-mediated translation (interpolated/pluralized lookups and miss walks) compute its chain through FallbackLocaleList#[], which dereferences SiteSetting.default_locale at line 17, so I18n now performs a database-backed settings read inside the translation path of every process type, not just web requests. Operators running Rails code against a database without the site_settings table (fresh-install bootstrap while db:migrate is still mid-run, rails runner or a recovery console on an empty DB) get ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid / PG::UndefinedTable raised out of an I18n lookup instead of the missing-translation marker; before this PR dev/test/rake had no fallbacks at all and production's config.i18n.fallbacks used I18n::Locale::Fallbacks, neither of which queried SiteSetting.

[ADVISORY] [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq fails to deduplicate the current locale against its Symbol twin because I18n.locale is a String on the common request path (set_locale assigns the raw SiteSetting.default_locale / user-locale strings, as shown in the adjacent app/controllers/application_controller.rb hunk), so a request whose locale equals the site default produces ['en', :en, :en].uniq => ['en', :en] instead of a two-element chain. Every web process runs I18n.ensure_loaded! twice for the primary locale (once as String, once as Symbol) and hands I18n::Backend::Fallbacks a chain containing the same locale twice, doubling preload work and adding a dead hop to every fallback miss walk; the extra locale dicts and lookups scale with worker count and go unnoticed because translation results still resolve correctly.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces three pieces of behavior-bearing logic — the FallbackLocaleList fallback-chain computation and its ensure_loaded! (lines 12-23), the TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded! preload patch in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb, and the ApplicationController#set_locale hook — with no test anywhere in the diff covering any of them. A regression in chain ordering (user locale -> site default -> en), dedup, or locale type handling ships silently because nothing in CI asserts the fallback list or that a key missing in locale A returns the site-default/English translation; sites would just see translation_missing markers again with no red build, and the String/Symbol duplication at line 17 is exactly the class of defect a one-line spec on FallbackLocaleList#[] would have caught before merge.

[BUG] ensure_loaded! calls I18n.ensure_loaded!, a method defined neither in this diff nor by the i18n gem — the only ensure_loaded! this diff adds lives on TranslateAccelerator (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62-65) and the I18n module has no delegation to its backend, so the bridge from I18n.ensure_loaded! to the backend method is missing from the diff. ApplicationController#set_locale (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:160) runs I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! on every request; with no definition of I18n.ensure_loaded! anywhere in the diff, this raises NoMethodError and turns every page and API call into a 500 — a full-site outage gated entirely on unstated out-of-diff wiring.

[ADVISORY] The diff ships a new global fallback architecture (FallbackLocaleList, backend module inclusion, per-request preload hook, removal of fallback config from three production environment files) with zero test files — a scan of the diff finds no spec/**, test/**, or *.spec.* additions covering any of it. The uncovered behaviors are exactly the load-bearing ones: chain ordering (user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en), that I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate is actually reached (TranslateAccelerator defines its own translate(key, *args) which shadows the included Fallbacks#translate(locale, key, options) unless its internal super passes the backend signature — nothing in the diff verifies the wiring), that ensure_loaded! preloads work, and that pluralization survived the consolidation of the deleted config/initializers/pluralization.rb into this initializer; a regression in any of these silently mis-renders every server-side string for non-English users.

[BUG] I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is wired only into the HTTP filter set_locale; no background path (Sidekiq mail jobs, rake tasks, console) ever preloads the fallback locales, and TranslateAccelerator#translate lazy-loads only config.locale, never the fallback locales. Discourse generates all email in Sidekiq jobs; a fresh worker whose first job is a notification for a 'de' user on a site with default_locale 'fr' has neither :fr nor :en translations loaded (I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate never loads, it only rescues MissingTranslationData down the chain), so the site-default and English fallback hops render 'translation missing: ...' strings in production emails — the PR's headline fallback silently fails for the entire background/mail server surface.

[ADVISORY] Moving fallback enablement out of the production-only environment files into an initializer turns fallbacks on in development and test, where config.i18n.fallbacks was never set before this diff. Developers lose their missing-translation signal: a key absent from a non-English locale's server.yml that previously rendered as a loud 'translation missing:' marker in dev/test now silently renders English, so the test suite can no longer catch untranslated or typo'd keys — the exact gap this feature papers over at runtime now also hides it at verification time, and translation regressions reach users of minority locales undetected.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] rebuilds the chain on every invocation — fresh 3-element array plus uniq, compact, to_sym, and a SiteSetting.default_locale read — and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate evaluates I18n.fallbacks[locale] on every lookup instead of the plain Hash lookup the old config.i18n.fallbacks = true provided. Every interpolated I18n.t call (the args.length > 0 no-cache path in TranslateAccelerator#translate) now pays array allocation and re-derivation per translated string on translation-heavy pages with hundreds of lookups per request; a per-locale memoized chain eliminates it, and the omission is a hot-path cost on every request of every high-traffic site.

[ADVISORY] The chain symbolizes SiteSetting.default_locale but not the incoming locale, so when I18n.locale is a String — which it is on the set_locale else-branch that assigns SiteSetting.default_locale, a String — a site whose default matches the user's locale yields a chain like ["de", :de, :en]. I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! iterates both "de" and :de, and TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!'s @loaded_locales.include? guard treats them as distinct, so load_locale parses the same server.de.yml twice and stores it under two type-identities, doubling per-locale parse cost and memory while one of the two chain entries is a dead lookup hop on every miss — the next change to locale handling has to reason about which of the two types actually resolves.

[BUG] The only call site that preloads the fallback-chain locales is ApplicationController#set_locale, so every server-side translation running outside an HTTP request — the Sidekiq jobs that render Discourse's emails, digests, and system messages — executes the new fallback chain against fallback locales that were never loaded. A mailer job rendering an email in the user's locale hits a key missing from that locale; the Fallbacks backend then tries SiteSetting.default_locale and :en, but neither was load_locale'd in the Sidekiq process (TranslateAccelerator#translate at lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 only lazy-loads config.locale), so the user is emailed raw 'translation missing: en.mailer_subject' text instead of the site-default/English fallback the feature exists to provide — the feature silently exists only for web-page rendering.

[BUG] The fallback chain makes translation results depend on the live per-site value of SiteSetting.default_locale (line 17), but the diff adds no cache keying or invalidation for the process-wide translation cache that TranslateAccelerator#translate front-runs on its no-args path (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:69), so fallback-resolved strings are stored under a cache key that cannot distinguish sites or setting changes. In a multisite deployment, two sites with different default locales share the per-process (locale, key) cache, so a user on site B whose locale is missing a key is served site A's fallback-language text; likewise, after an admin changes default_locale, previously cached fallback-baked strings keep rendering in the old language until process restart.

[ADVISORY] The new ensure_loaded! centralizes the guard-then-load pattern, but the adjacent translate keeps its own inline copy (line 68, `load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`) instead of delegating, and the two copies already disagree — ensure_loaded! defensively initializes @loaded_locales while translate dereferences it unguarded. The next change to the loading policy — a mutex for the multithreaded first-load race, or logging on first load — must be replicated in two places and one will be missed; replacing translate's guard with ensure_loaded!(config.locale) deletes the duplicated branch outright.

[ADVISORY] Two adjacent backend-module includes attach by incompatible strategies — Pluralization is pinned to the I18n::Backend::Simple constant (line 5) while Fallbacks is bound to whatever class I18n.backend happens to be at initializer time (line 9) — so the two behaviors detach under different conditions. A plugin or test harness that reassigns I18n.backend (a chain wrapper, a stub) silently runs with pluralization but without fallbacks, or vice versa, depending on whether the assignment happens before or after this initializer; because neither detachment raises, the next contributor spends hours tracing why fallbacks work in one boot path and not another.

[ADVISORY] The new non-trivial fallback semantics — the user-locale → site-default → English ordering and uniq/compact dedup (lines 13-18), FallbackLocaleList's Hash#[] contract with i18n's Fallbacks backend, and the ensure_loaded! preloading handshake with TranslateAccelerator — ship with no test anywhere in the diff. A future edit that reorders the chain, drops the :en last resort, or breaks the ensure_loaded! protocol changes the rendered language of server-side strings for entire locale groups and merges undetected, because nothing in the suite pins the contract this initializer creates.

[BUG] Fallback-chain locale preloading is owned exclusively by the HTTP request lifecycle — `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` runs only in set_locale, while the lazy accelerator in translate_accelerator.rb loads only the current locale (`translate` -> `load_locale(config.locale)`), so every non-request process executes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` over backend locales that were never loaded. All Discourse mail is rendered in Sidekiq processes that never run set_locale: on a site whose default_locale is not English, a user-locale email missing a key falls through the unloaded site-default leg and delivers English text (or a raw 'translation missing' marker in a fresh process that never loaded :en) instead of the site-default language, and whether the fallback works flips depending on which locales happened to load earlier in that process's lifetime.

[BUG] Removing `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` silently drops the standard I18n::Locale::Fallbacks parent-language chain (pt-BR->pt, zh-TW->zh) from production; the replacement chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]` in config/initializers/i18n.rb has no parent-language leg at all. Regional-locale users lose existing production behavior: a pt_BR user on an English-default site currently gets Portuguese via the pt leg for keys missing in pt_BR; after this change they get English — a user-visible regression for every Discourse regional locale, shipped with no data-driven place to re-add the parent leg (the TODO only mentions cross-variant fallbacks).

[BUG] `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every fallback computation, putting a DB-backed settings read on the translation-miss path of every process, including contexts where the site_settings table or connection does not exist (first `db:migrate`/`db:bootstrap` boot, `rails runner` against an unbuilt database). A missing translation key during a DB-less boot context that previously returned a 'translation missing' marker now raises `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (relation "site_settings" does not exist) out of `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`, aborting the boot or rake task instead of degrading to the marker.

[BUG] The fallback chain bakes the per-site value `SiteSetting.default_locale` into results memoized in the process-global translation cache (translate_accelerator.rb's `translate` caches per (locale, key) on the shared I18n module), so identical cache keys hold site-specific fallback text on multisite installs. On a multisite install where site A defaults to :fr and site B to :es, a German user's lookup of a key missing in :de caches French text under (de, key) while serving site A; site B's German users then hit that cache entry and receive site A's French text instead of site B's Spanish — wrong-language content crossing tenant boundaries with no translation-override involvement.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides `[]` to ignore the underlying store, so the inherited write API that i18n documents for custom fallbacks (`I18n.fallbacks[:zh_TW] = [:zh_TW, :zh_CN]`, `merge!`) accepts writes that no read path ever consults. A plugin or operator configuring per-language fallbacks — the exact zh_TW/zh_CN enhancement this file's own TODO anticipates — gets a silent no-op: the assignment succeeds, the lookup path never sees it, translations keep resolving without the custom leg, and no error surfaces the loss.

[ADVISORY] The cached no-args `translate` path stores fallback-resolved text under the requesting locale's cache entry, while Discourse's translation-override invalidation is keyed by the overridden locale's (locale, key) pair, so an override saved for the fallback locale never evicts entries that were populated from that fallback. When an admin edits English copy on a multilingual site, users browsing in other locales keep seeing the pre-edit English text — served from (their_locale, key) cache entries written via fallback — until the process restarts, so the override appears applied for English users but not for everyone else.

[ADVISORY] `ensure_loaded!` is defined only on the concrete FallbackLocaleList class and invoked unguarded from ApplicationController#set_locale, hard-coupling every request to this initializer's exact class being installed as `I18n.fallbacks`. Any plugin or operator installing a fallbacks object through i18n's documented customization points (`config.i18n.fallbacks = {...}`, or `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks.new`) — which need not respond to `ensure_loaded!` — makes set_locale raise NoMethodError in a before_action on every request, bricking the site instead of degrading to untranslated keys.

[ADVISORY] The chain literal normalizes its second element (`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`) but leaves the first element raw, so when the backend passes the request locale as the String Discourse negotiates ('en'), `[locale, ...].uniq` keeps both 'en' and :en — String and Symbol are not uniq-equal. On sites where the request locale equals the default locale, every missing-key lookup executes a redundant duplicate backend miss lookup on the uncached args path (`I18n.t(key, count: n)`), and the developer who implements the per-language TODO must handle two encodings of every locale or the custom leg silently never matches.

[BUG] FallbackLocaleList#[] builds the chain from the raw request locale plus the Symbolized site default ([locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq), so uniq fails to collapse the pair whenever the request locale is the String form that set_locale assigns in its default branch (I18n.locale = ... SiteSetting.default_locale), leaving the site's primary locale twice in the chain (e.g. ["en", :en]). ensure_loaded! (line 21) then calls the accelerator's load_locale twice — once for the String and once for the Symbol — and the @loaded_locales include? guard in translate_accelerator.rb treats the two forms as distinct, so every process parses and caches the site's hottest translation tree twice and holds a duplicate copy in per-process memory; each missing-key lookup additionally walks a redundant duplicate hop.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes the chain on every backend translate — a SiteSetting.default_locale read, a to_sym, and a three-element Array plus uniq/compact allocations — with no memoization into the Hash storage it subclasses, while I18n::Backend::Fallbacks computes I18n.fallbacks[locale] up front for every lookup because the list must contain the original locale. Every interpolated I18n.t in production (the args-present path that always reaches the backend) now pays a SiteSetting read plus fresh allocations where the deleted config.i18n.fallbacks = true wiring served the same list from I18n::Locale::Fallbacks' memoized per-locale map; high-traffic sites absorb extra CPU and GC pressure on every request's translation calls.

[ADVISORY] Centralizing fallback configuration in an environment-agnostic initializer while deleting only the production-scoped config.i18n.fallbacks = true lines (config/environments/production.rb, profile.rb, cloud66) silently extends fallback behavior to development and test, which previously surfaced missing keys as 'translation missing' markers. Developers and plugin/theme translators lose the only environment that loudly reported absent keys: a partially translated locale now silently renders English/default text during development and in the test suite, so translation gaps — including ones introduced by newly added keys — ship to production undetected.

[ADVISORY] The declared load-order dependency ('order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb') is enforced only by a comment plus the accident that '02-...' sorts lexicographically before 'i18n.rb', with no mechanical guard in the file. A routine rename of either initializer (e.g. renumbering '10-i18n.rb' or renaming the freedom_patches initializer) silently reverses the backend-patch order the author explicitly depends on; the resulting translation/fallback misbehavior produces no boot error, so production sites serve subtly wrong strings until someone re-reads this comment.

[ADVISORY] Replacing the standard I18n::Locale::Fallbacks object with a Hash subclass whose [] ignores stored values silently degrades the documented i18n fallbacks configuration surface: I18n.fallbacks.map(:ca => :es) becomes Hash#map over an always-empty store (a silent no-op) and fallback registrations via []= are never read back. Plugin/gem authors and future core changes that register per-locale fallbacks through the standard API — exactly the per-language fallback refinement this file's own TODO contemplates (zh_TW to zh_CN) — get silent no-ops instead of configuration taking effect, with no error pointing at this class.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces behavior-bearing logic — FallbackLocaleList#[] chain construction, FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, the accelerator's ensure_loaded!, and the per-request warm call added to ApplicationController#set_locale — and no test anywhere in the diff exercises any of it. A regression in the chain construction (the String/Symbol uniq gap shipped in this very diff is precisely the class of bug a chain spec would catch) silently changes string rendering for every non-English site, and because fallbacks exist to hide missing-key markers, users see wrong-language text with neither a test nor a boot-time signal.

[BUG] Installing FallbackLocaleList as the process-global I18n.fallbacks makes every backend translation resolve its chain through SiteSetting.default_locale — a DB-backed site setting — so I18n.t now raises in any context without an established site connection where it previously resolved fallbacks via the pure-Ruby I18n::Locale::Fallbacks with no database dependency. On multisite installs, rake tasks, `rails runner` scripts, and any code that translates before a site connection is established crash with a no-connection error instead of returning a translated string (I18n::Backend::Fallbacks, now included into the backend at line 9, calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] before every lookup, so the SiteSetting read at line 17 is unavoidable for all I18n.t calls); before this diff, production's `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` produced a locale-subtag-only chain that worked without a DB.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but its overridden [] never reads stored entries, so the standard write-then-read contract of the public I18n.fallbacks surface (I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...], honored by the stock I18n::Locale::Fallbacks this replaces in production) silently accepts and then ignores the stored value. Any plugin author or operator who configures per-locale fallback chains via the documented I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...] API gets a silent no-op — no error and no effect — while the hardcoded [user_locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] chain applies instead; the TODO on lines 15-16 invites exactly this extension, so the next developer implementing it will write a mapping that does nothing.

[BUG] The new fallback-preloading hook `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is wired into exactly one call site — the web-request path in `set_locale` — while the fallback machinery the diff enables globally (`I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` plus `FallbackLocaleList`) is process-global, so server-side translations executed outside controller dispatch run with fallback locales that are never loaded. The accelerator's `translate` only loads `config.locale` (translate_accelerator.rb:69 `load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`); in a Sidekiq worker rendering a localized email, a key missing in the user's locale falls through `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` to the site-default and `:en` locales, which were never `load_locale`d in that process, so the chain exhausts and the user-facing email ships with literal `translation missing: …` fragments instead of the translated text — the feature this PR exists to provide silently fails in every non-request context (fresh job processes never run set_locale).

[ADVISORY] Installing `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` unconditionally in the initializer turns fallbacks on in development and test, where `config.i18n.fallbacks` was previously unset and Rails deliberately enables fallbacks only in production (the diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from production.rb/profile.rb/cloud66 but adds global behavior everywhere). Developers and translation contributors reviewing untranslated or partially translated locales in development now see silently-resolved English text instead of the `translation missing: …` markers that previously surfaced, so missing keys are first discovered by end users in production rather than during development; any test asserting on missing-translation behavior also changes meaning.

[ADVISORY] `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` mixes the String `I18n.locale` (assigned directly from the String `SiteSetting.default_locale` / `user.locale` in `set_locale`, visible in the diff context) with Symbol entries, and `uniq` uses equality, so the chain for an English site is `["en", :en]` rather than a single entry. `I18n.ensure_loaded!` loads English twice per process under distinct locale keys — the accelerator's `@loaded_locales` and per-locale translation stores hold both `"en"` and `:en` — doubling the memory of the largest translation tree in every web and background process and duplicating fallback iteration for each missing key; the same String/Symbol split applies to any site-default locale pair.

[BUG] The only code path that preloads the fallback-chain locales is ApplicationController#set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, so in any process that renders localized text without passing through a web controller (sidekiq email/notification/digest jobs using I18n.with_locale, rake, console) the fallback lookups hit locales that were never loaded in that process. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate performs each fallback attempt via `super(fallback, key, options)`, which goes straight into Simple#translate and bypasses TranslateAccelerator's `load_locale(config.locale)` guard (that guard only ever loads the primary locale). In a sidekiq process, which never runs set_locale, the newly-added middle chain entry SiteSetting.default_locale is never loaded for non-English-default sites: a background email for a user with locale ru on a site whose default is de renders English (or a 'translation missing' string on a fresh process where :en is also not yet loaded) instead of the configured German fallback — silently, with no error logged, because a fallback miss is indistinguishable from a genuinely absent key. Pre-PR production fallback chains were [locale, I18n.default_locale] and worked in jobs because :en loads on the first ordinary translate; this diff adds the site-default entry that is structurally dead in all background rendering.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides `[]` to always recompute `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, so the documented i18n customization API `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]` becomes a silent no-op: Hash#[]= is not overridden, the write succeeds, and the stored value is never read back. Any Discourse plugin or vendored gem that follows the standard per-locale fallback-customization idiom gets zero effect with no error and no warning, shipping the wrong fallback order to end users; a maintainer debugging the chain will read the initializer, see a Hash, and reasonably assume stored fallbacks apply. The strongest rebuttal — 'core never writes to I18n.fallbacks' — describes today's core only; the initializer deliberately swapped out the public fallbacks object for a look-alike, and out-of-tree callers are the ones this family exists to protect.

[ADVISORY] `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` enables the fallback chain unconditionally in every environment, whereas previously only production/profile/cloud66 enabled fallbacks (the config was removed from production.rb, profile.rb and the cloud66 file), so dev and test environments switch from surfacing missing translations to silently swallowing them. Before this diff, a missing key in a non-English locale raised/returned a visible 'translation missing' marker in dev and test — the primary detection surface for incomplete plugin/theme locale files, which core's yml-parity specs do not cover. After it, the same lookup returns English text and reports success, so developers and CI specs no longer notice incomplete locale coverage and the gaps ship to production. The rebuttal 'dev now shows what production shows' inverts the canary role dev/test played pre-PR and leaves no environment that surfaces the failure.

[ADVISORY] The new `ensure_loaded!` hand-rolls the same `unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` guard that `translate` (line 67) already implements inline, so the loaded-locales idempotence invariant is now enforced at two parallel call sites in the same class instead of being centralized inside load_locale (or by having translate call the new ensure_loaded!). The next change to locale bookkeeping — normalizing keys to symbols, adding synchronization, or rolling back @loaded_locales on a failed load — must be replicated at every guard site; missing one makes a guard permanently false (locale files re-parsed on every request: latency/CPU burn) or permanently true (locales never load: missing-translation output of exactly the kind the sibling finding describes). The author's counter — 'the guards are cheap and correct today' — concedes the point: the finding is about change-safety of a freshly duplicated invariant, and translate's guard line is directly replaceable by `ensure_loaded!(config.locale)`, a one-place consolidation this diff was ideally positioned to make.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The declared load-order dependency ('order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb') is enforced only by a comment plus the accident that '02-...' sorts lexicographically before 'i18n.rb', with no mechanical guard in the file. adjudication.rationale: The new initializer `config/initializers/i18n.rb` explicitly declares a load-order dependency via comment (`# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`) but contains no code-level guard/enforcement. Rails initializer order is filename-based, so it currently relies on lexicographic sorting (e.g., `02-...` before `i18n.rb`). If either file is renamed/renumbered, the include/patch order (e.g., `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` and `I18n.fallbacks = ...`) could change without any boot-time failure. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Replacing the standard I18n::Locale::Fallbacks object with a Hash subclass whose [] ignores stored values silently degrades the documented i18n fallbacks configuration surface: I18n.fallbacks.map(:ca => :es) becomes Hash#map over an always-empty store (a silent no-op) and fallback registrations via []= are never read back. Plugin/gem authors and future core changes that register per-locale fallbacks through the standard API — exactly the per-language fallback refinement this file's own TODO contemplates (zh_TW to zh_CN) — get silent no-ops instead of configuration taking effect, with no error pointing at this class.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the standard `I18n.fallbacks` object with `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` whose `[]` always returns a computed array and never consults stored mappings. This means any per-locale fallback registrations written into the hash (e.g., via `[]=` or the standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks#map` configuration API) will not be read back by `[]`, so such configuration becomes a silent no-op. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff introduces behavior-bearing logic — FallbackLocaleList#[] chain construction, FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, the accelerator's ensure_loaded!, and the per-request warm call added to ApplicationController#set_locale — and no test anywhere in the diff exercises any of it. A regression in the chain construction (the String/Symbol uniq gap shipped in this very diff is precisely the class of bug a chain spec would catch) silently changes string rendering for every non-English site, and because fallbacks exist to hide missing-key markers, users see wrong-language text with neither a test nor a boot-time signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple pieces of new, behavior-bearing i18n logic (new `config/initializers/i18n.rb` with `FallbackLocaleList#[]` and `#ensure_loaded!`, a new `ensure_loaded!` method in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`, and a new per-request call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`). The finding’s specific “no test in the diff for this new logic” claim is directly supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Installing FallbackLocaleList as the process-global I18n.fallbacks makes every backend translation resolve its chain through SiteSetting.default_locale — a DB-backed site setting — so I18n.t now raises in any context without an established site connection where it previously resolved fallbacks via the pure-Ruby I18n::Locale::Fallbacks with no database dependency. On multisite installs, rake tasks, `rails runner` scripts, and any code that translates before a site connection is established crash with a no-connection error instead of returning a translated string (I18n::Backend::Fallbacks, now included into the backend at line 9, calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] before every lookup, so the SiteSetting read at line 17 is unavoidable for all I18n.t calls); before this diff, production's `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` produced a locale-subtag-only chain that worked without a DB.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces Rails’ environment-level `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` with a process-global `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` (config/initializers/i18n.rb) whose `[]` method unconditionally reads `SiteSetting.default_locale`. Because the initializer also includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` into the backend, fallback resolution will consult `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`, making the `SiteSetting` access part of the fallback chain computation. This introduces a new hard dependency on `SiteSetting` for fallback computation that did not exist when using the built-in fallbacks enabled via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true`, and can break translation calls in contexts where `SiteSetting` is not available/initialized (e.g., before site selection/connection).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but its overridden [] never reads stored entries, so the standard write-then-read contract of the public I18n.fallbacks surface (I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...], honored by the stock I18n::Locale::Fallbacks this replaces in production) silently accepts and then ignores the stored value. Any plugin author or operator who configures per-locale fallback chains via the documented I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...] API gets a silent no-op — no error and no effect — while the hardcoded [user_locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] chain applies instead; the TODO on lines 15-16 invites exactly this extension, so the next developer implementing it will write a mapping that does nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides `[](locale)` to always return `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and never consults any stored hash entries. Since `[]=` is still inherited from Hash, callers could write `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = ...` and it would be silently ignored on reads. The diff doesn’t show any in-repo code relying on `[]=` (so a concrete breakage can’t be proven here), but it is a real API/extension trap created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new fallback-preloading hook `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is wired into exactly one call site — the web-request path in `set_locale` — while the fallback machinery the diff enables globally (`I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` plus `FallbackLocaleList`) is process-global, so server-side translations executed outside controller dispatch run with fallback locales that are never loaded. The accelerator's `translate` only loads `config.locale` (translate_accelerator.rb:69 `load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`); in a Sidekiq worker rendering a localized email, a key missing in the user's locale falls through `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` to the site-default and `:en` locales, which were never `load_locale`d in that process, so the chain exhausts and the user-facing email ships with literal `translation missing: …` fragments instead of the translated text — the feature this PR exists to provide silently fails in every non-request context (fresh job processes never run set_locale).

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` only into `ApplicationController#set_locale` (new call added there). The new fallback setup is global (`I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` included and `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`), so any translations executed in non-controller contexts (e.g., background jobs, rake tasks) will not run this preload hook unless they call it elsewhere (no other call sites shown). However, the finding’s claimed concrete failure mode (“fallback chain exhausts and emails ship with `translation missing`”) can’t be conclusively verified from the diff alone because it depends on how `TranslateAccelerator#translate` interacts with the I18n fallback backend and whether fallback lookups already trigger locale loading implicitly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Installing `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` unconditionally in the initializer turns fallbacks on in development and test, where `config.i18n.fallbacks` was previously unset and Rails deliberately enables fallbacks only in production (the diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from production.rb/profile.rb/cloud66 but adds global behavior everywhere). Developers and translation contributors reviewing untranslated or partially translated locales in development now see silently-resolved English text instead of the `translation missing: …` markers that previously surfaced, so missing keys are first discovered by end users in production rather than during development; any test asserting on missing-translation behavior also changes meaning.

adjudication.rationale: The new initializer `config/initializers/i18n.rb` unconditionally includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, which applies in all environments. The diff also removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from production/profile/cloud66, shifting fallback behavior from being explicitly enabled only in those env files to being globally installed. This can change how missing translations surface (e.g., falling back to `SiteSetting.default_locale`/`:en` instead of showing missing-translation markers) in development/test compared to prior behavior, even if the intent is to standardize fallbacks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` mixes the String `I18n.locale` (assigned directly from the String `SiteSetting.default_locale` / `user.locale` in `set_locale`, visible in the diff context) with Symbol entries, and `uniq` uses equality, so the chain for an English site is `["en", :en]` rather than a single entry. `I18n.ensure_loaded!` loads English twice per process under distinct locale keys — the accelerator's `@loaded_locales` and per-locale translation stores hold both `"en"` and `:en` — doubling the memory of the largest translation tree in every web and background process and duplicating fallback iteration for each missing key; the same String/Symbol split applies to any site-default locale pair.

[BUG] The only code path that preloads the fallback-chain locales is ApplicationController#set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, so in any process that renders localized text without passing through a web controller (sidekiq email/notification/digest jobs using I18n.with_locale, rake, console) the fallback lookups hit locales that were never loaded in that process. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate performs each fallback attempt via `super(fallback, key, options)`, which goes straight into Simple#translate and bypasses TranslateAccelerator's `load_locale(config.locale)` guard (that guard only ever loads the primary locale). In a sidekiq process, which never runs set_locale, the newly-added middle chain entry SiteSetting.default_locale is never loaded for non-English-default sites: a background email for a user with locale ru on a site whose default is de renders English (or a 'translation missing' string on a fresh process where :en is also not yet loaded) instead of the configured German fallback — silently, with no error logged, because a fallback miss is indistinguishable from a genuinely absent key. Pre-PR production fallback chains were [locale, I18n.default_locale] and worked in jobs because :en loads on the first ordinary translate; this diff adds the site-default entry that is structurally dead in all background rendering.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a custom fallback chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, but the only added call that proactively loads that chain is in `ApplicationController#set_locale` via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. Nothing in the diff shows analogous loading for non-controller code paths (jobs/rake/console), and `translate_accelerator.rb` still only auto-loads `config.locale` in `translate`, not the fallback locales. Given the new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` implementation relies on being invoked, background processes can plausibly miss loading `SiteSetting.default_locale`/`:en` and therefore have incorrect/missing fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides `[]` to always recompute `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, so the documented i18n customization API `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]` becomes a silent no-op: Hash#[]= is not overridden, the write succeeds, and the stored value is never read back. Any Discourse plugin or vendored gem that follows the standard per-locale fallback-customization idiom gets zero effect with no error and no warning, shipping the wrong fallback order to end users; a maintainer debugging the chain will read the initializer, see a Hash, and reasonably assume stored fallbacks apply. The strongest rebuttal — 'core never writes to I18n.fallbacks' — describes today's core only; the initializer deliberately swapped out the public fallbacks object for a look-alike, and out-of-tree callers are the ones this family exists to protect.

adjudication.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `def [](locale)` to always return a freshly computed `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and never consults the underlying Hash storage. Since `Hash#[]=` is not overridden, any caller doing the standard `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]` will successfully write but the value will never be read back (silent no-op). The diff also assigns `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, so this behavior applies globally and can break expected i18n fallback customization semantics for out-of-tree code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` enables the fallback chain unconditionally in every environment, whereas previously only production/profile/cloud66 enabled fallbacks (the config was removed from production.rb, profile.rb and the cloud66 file), so dev and test environments switch from surfacing missing translations to silently swallowing them. Before this diff, a missing key in a non-English locale raised/returned a visible 'translation missing' marker in dev and test — the primary detection surface for incomplete plugin/theme locale files, which core's yml-parity specs do not cover. After it, the same lookup returns English text and reports success, so developers and CI specs no longer notice incomplete locale coverage and the gaps ship to production. The rebuttal 'dev now shows what production shows' inverts the canary role dev/test played pre-PR and leaves no environment that surfaces the failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `config/initializers/i18n.rb` which unconditionally mixes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` into the backend and sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, and `FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns a chain including `:en`. Since initializers run in all environments, this makes fallbacks active globally, whereas the explicit `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were only present (and are now removed) in `production.rb`, `profile.rb`, and the cloud66 production config. The concern that this can mask missing non-English translations by falling back to English is directly supported by the new fallback chain, though the exact prior behavior in dev/test isn’t fully shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `ensure_loaded!` hand-rolls the same `unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` guard that `translate` (line 67) already implements inline, so the loaded-locales idempotence invariant is now enforced at two parallel call sites in the same class instead of being centralized inside load_locale (or by having translate call the new ensure_loaded!). The next change to locale bookkeeping — normalizing keys to symbols, adding synchronization, or rolling back @loaded_locales on a failed load — must be replicated at every guard site; missing one makes a guard permanently false (locale files re-parsed on every request: latency/CPU burn) or permanently true (locales never load: missing-translation output of exactly the kind the sibling finding describes). The author's counter — 'the guards are cheap and correct today' — concedes the point: the finding is about change-safety of a freshly duplicated invariant, and translate's guard line is directly replaceable by `ensure_loaded!(config.locale)`, a one-place consolidation this diff was ideally positioned to make.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb the diff adds ensure_loaded!(locale) which implements the same guard pattern as translate already has inline: `load_locale locale unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` (new method) vs `load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` (existing translate). The new helper is not used to replace the existing guard, so the locale-loaded idempotence logic is now duplicated across two call sites, increasing maintenance/change-safety risk if @loaded_locales semantics or locale normalization changes later. This is a concrete, diff-grounded design concern rather than an immediately verifiable runtime bug.
